input.purpose: Life-safety emergency: give gas leak safety advice immediately and confirm the household is safe
input.talking_points:
- This is the agency maintenance team following your call about the gas smell.
- If the smell is strong, everyone (and any pets) should leave the house now. Do NOT use light switches, sockets, the cooker, doorbells, or anything that could spark; no naked flames or smoking.
- If safe to do so on the way out, turn off the gas at the meter (lever turned so it is crossways to the pipe) and leave doors/windows open.
- Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 now, from outside the property. It is free and they will attend to make safe.
- Sadie's headache can be a sign of carbon monoxide - she should get fresh air and, if she feels dizzy, sick, confused or the headache worsens, call NHS 111 or 999.
- Ask: has anyone already called 0800 111 999? Is everyone out of the property / safe? Any CO alarm sounding? Any pets?
- Tell them: we have raised an emergency ticket and escalated to the property manager; a Gas Safe registered engineer will be arranged for any follow-up repair. They will not be charged for this - it is the landlord's responsibility.
- Ask them to tell us what the gas emergency engineer says/does (e.g. appliance capped or meter isolated) and keep us updated.
